author.name: Jrk Bgrt (pseudonymous, real identity not publicly resolved)

target_format: candidate answer string X; password = sha256(X) hex; decrypts an OpenSSL Salted__ AES-256-CBC blob printed on the final page; plaintext reduces to a 32-byte private key; uncompressed secp256k1 public key; P2PKH address

derivation.summary: candidate answer to sha256 password to AES-256-CBC decrypt of the small final-page blob to a 32-byte private key (one of 4 standard readings of the plaintext) to uncompressed P2PKH address
derivation.certified_against: two independent parts: the escrow's own on-chain public key (from its 2024-04-24 spending transaction) hashes byte-exact to its address; a self-made OpenSSL-compatible AES-256-CBC round trip decrypts correctly with the right password and produces no valid padding with a wrong one. No end-to-end vector exists because X is unsolved.

difficulty_note: the stage chain to the final page is fully solved and reproducible; the 256-symbol object the puzzle's own Bifid step produces has been tested as a direct 32-byte key reduction across roughly 335.7 million candidates with 0 match; the small blob's AES-decrypt pipeline is certified but no password has been found; a further 116,043-candidate replay of historical literal password guesses is also negative and explicitly partial (dynamically-constructed candidates from the same scripts were never replayed); the larger Dualite blob, which likely gates the second address, has never had any password tested against it

leads.title: replay the dynamically-constructed candidates a filter bug never reached
determine whether the 256-symbol object is the right target at all
identify the single tool reportedly used to build every phase
follow esrever, the earliest published hint
